races.name: QuinnBet Best Odds Guaranteed 'Confined' Handicap

runners_data.name: Leonato
runners_data.note: A hold-up 3yo from George Boughey's yard who steps up significantly in trip from 8-10f to 1m6f — the distance question is the biggest query here, and his recent form of 9-3-4 offers limited encouragement; Jack Callan (3lb claimer) brings a small weight advantage but the horse's stamina at this far longer trip remains unproven.

runners_data.name: Kelly Burn
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's 3yo has form over 10-12f and is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this field, which means Cieren Fallon can dictate entirely unchallenged — her STYLE_FIT tag signals she is stretching into a front-running role, but in a four-runner field with no rivals willing to race prominently, she is unlikely to be pressured and may exploit this tactical advantage fully.

runners_data.name: Mountbatten
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's operation is in clinical form and this 3yo won over 12f on stamina ground just eight days ago, making the quick turnaround a deliberate stable move rather than a concern; Stevie Donohoe has a good understanding of the yard's horses, and the step up to 1m6f looks a natural progression for a horse whose profile screams staying-trip improver.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Astolat
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type from Charlie Fellowes' yard whose natural style has her arriving late, but with three other hold-up runners in the race she will not be alone at the back — her sim-going record of 2 from 5 with no wins or places on good is a red flag on this surface, and her OR of 57 leaves her with plenty to find on ratings; Saffie Osborne takes the ride but the overall profile is one of a horse who needs things to fall right.

races.paceDynamic: Kelly Burn is the one confirmed front-runner in a four-runner field and should be able to dictate terms unchallenged from the outset over 1m6f on good-to-firm ground at Yarmouth, setting a measured, controlled pace rather than a pressured gallop. With Leonato, Mountbatten, and Queen Of Astolat all carrying hold-up or deep hold-up profiles, there is no genuine rival to contest the lead, meaning Kelly Burn can dictate tempo entirely on Cieren Fallon's terms. The field does contain more hold-up types than the shape can accommodate naturally — Queen Of Astolat, a true hold-up runner, has been redistributed to midfield on the map because there is simply no front-running competition to push Kelly Burn back. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader controlling pace over a stamina trip on fast ground — strongly favours horses who can travel handy and sustain their effort, and the most interesting threats will come from whichever hold-up runner can produce the sharpest late thrust once the pace inevitably steadies in the straight.

scenarios.title: Muddling Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and the race turns into a sprint finish from two furlongs out with no meaningful gallop.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses completely and the race turns into a sprint finish from two furlongs out with no meaningful gallop.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Ties Up Late

watchPoints.text: Kelly Burn's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if Cieren Fallon gets her into a rhythm and the others don't press, the race could be over as a contest before the final bend.

Mountbatten's eight-day turnaround is unusually quick even for Sir Mark Prescott — watch for any market drift that might signal the stable is viewing this as a fitness run rather than a winning mission.

Leonato faces a sharp trip increase from 8-10f to 1m6f and his stamina at this extreme distance is completely unknown — if he fades badly it could gift the result to whoever is travelling best at the two-furlong pole.

Queen Of Astolat's going record on good ground is poor (0 wins, 0 places from 2 runs) and today's good-to-firm conditions at Yarmouth may not bring out the best in her — worth monitoring in the market for any sign of confidence from connections.

With only four runners, any trouble in running is minimal, but Queen Of Astolat's redistribution to midfield means she may not settle into her natural rhythm — watch how Saffie Osborne positions her in the first half-mile as a guide to whether she is travelling comfortably.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gorgeous Mr George
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer whose single course win at this trip on Good ground is a direct asset here; trainer Dylan Cunha has 1 winner from 28 recent runners (T14) suggesting modest current form, and the 5lb claimer Taryn Langley carries some weight risk, but the horse's profile suits tracking Ya Karim closely.

runners_data.name: Distinct Spirit
runners_data.note: Returned after a 263-day absence looking to rediscover the 7f Good-ground win that marks her best form; she is a naturally forward-going filly who will find herself unable to get as close to the pace as she'd prefer given the crowded front ranks, which is a genuine tactical inconvenience for her chances.

runners_data.name: Daring Legend
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has run creditably at this trip on Good ground before, but recent runs are mostly over 6-7f and she will need the mile to be strongly run to allow her closing style to function; trainer Mark Pattinson has a quiet 14-day record (0/5) and the tongue-tie adds an equipment variable.

runners_data.name: North View
runners_data.note: Experienced hold-up performer with pace handicap history at 7-8f on Good and Standard, but his finishing position stats (sim-going: 6/15) reveal he is only a marginal threat when pace is fair; Sean Levey is a quality booking but the combination of a pedestrian pace and a flat track could blunt the challenge.

runners_data.name: Berry Clever
runners_data.note: In good current form with a 7f Good-ground win in recent memory and a high style-fit score for a prominent runner; shunted further back than ideal because of the crowded front, which means De Sousa will have to make a decision early about whether to commit upfront or accept a midfield berth, complicating race-day tactics.

runners_data.name: Luzon Heights
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old whose 5-run form string includes wins and placed efforts at 8f on Good and Standard, giving her the distance profile that suits this test precisely; Cieren Fallon is an astute booking for a horse that should track Ya Karim and poses one of the more credible prominent threats.

runners_data.name: Peel Park
runners_data.note: Roger Varian-trained three-year-old who has shown some quality in the form book but recent runs have returned mostly mid-pack finishes on Good ground; the blinkers are already a fixture in her headgear record (hg:b) so no freshness benefit there, and her 8/8 sim-going record suggests she handles the conditions without excelling.

runners_data.name: Kaori
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly dropping back from 10f to 1m for George Boughey, whose 14-day record is active (7/34); the step-down in trip is interesting as she could prove better served by this distance, but with only 1 placed run from 4 on similar going, she remains unproven in this specific context and Jack Callan's 3lb claim is a small positive.

runners_data.name: Ya Karim
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won over 7f on Good ground and sets the pace framework for the entire race; the [STYLE_FIT] tag acknowledges she may not get the truly dominant lead position if rivals crowd her early, but given the absence of a genuine challenger, she is highly likely to dictate terms — her ability to then quicken is the key question.

races.paceDynamic: Ya Karim is the one confirmed front-runner here and, crucially, faces no serious pressure from a rival willing to sit on her girth — she should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this flat Yarmouth mile on Good to Firm ground. Luzon Heights, Gorgeous Mr George, and Peel Park are all prominent types who will push forward behind her, creating a natural pecking order through the early stages rather than a war for supremacy. This field contains more forward-going, prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions — Distinct Spirit and Berry Clever are genuine prominent racers by nature but have been mapped to midfield because the lead and near-lead slots are already occupied by Ya Karim and the other prominent quartet, meaning those two are likely to race slightly further back than they would ideally choose. With Ya Karim able to bowl along uncontested at a sustainable clip, this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer who can track the pace within striking distance and quicken off a fair tempo — true hold-up horses will be asked to find too much ground in the final two furlongs on a flat, galloping track that typically rewards those travelling close to the pace.

scenarios.title: Ya Karim Controls, Prominent Pounces

scenarios.body: If Ya Karim leads at a fair but uncontested tempo and a stalking prominent horse picks her off in the final furlong.

scenarios.title: Midfield Types Mount Late Run

scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types refuse to settle and a proper pace battle develops that leaves the front group vulnerable to closers.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent types refuse to settle and a proper pace battle develops that leaves the front group vulnerable to closers.

watchPoints.text: Ya Karim's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the race's central variable — if she is tracked very tightly by Luzon Heights or Gorgeous Mr George from the outset, watch whether she is forced to quicken earlier than ideal, which would compromise her stamina over this mile.

Distinct Spirit and Berry Clever are both natural prominent racers who will find their forward instincts frustrated by a congested front rank — watch for early jostling in the first two furlongs as De Sousa and Osborne decide whether to commit or drop back, as that decision will determine whether they are competitive at all.

Luzon Heights has the most directly relevant distance and going profile in the field and Cieren Fallon is likely to position her right on Ya Karim's quarters — if she travels fluently there, she becomes the primary danger to the leader and any drift in the market should be treated as significant.

North View and Kaori are the two genuine hold-up horses and their chances hinge entirely on whether the pace is strong enough to bring them into the race late — on a flat Yarmouth mile with an uncontested leader, watch in-running whether the field bunches or strings out, as bunching signals a slow tempo that kills their chance.

The Good to Firm going report (confirmed for the 11:30) is important for Daring Legend, who wears a tongue-tie and has mixed recent form on this ground over shorter trips — watch to see whether she travels with any fluency before halfway, as a sluggish early move would confirm she is unlikely to factor.

races.name: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Handicap

runners_data.name: Rokuni
runners_data.note: Struggled badly in recent form (600-09), has no wins or places on similar going in 9 outings on turf, and is a genuine hold-up type whose chance depends entirely on a strong pace materialising and a clean late run — neither is guaranteed here.

runners_data.name: Sunset In Paris
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old returning after 101 days off with a jockey change, trainer at 0/7 over 14 days, and all relevant form on Tapeta at 10f — good-to-firm turf at Yarmouth after a long break is a significant ask, and its natural hold-up style is squeezed by the field composition.

runners_data.name: Zafaan
runners_data.note: Lengthy absence of 302 days (41 since a Flat entry) is a major unknown, trainer at 0/7 over 14 days, and though it has a win and four places on similar going over longer trips, dropping back from 16f to 10f means it must deploy its hold-up style from a more forward position than suits it naturally.

runners_data.name: Hunting Berries
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3-year-old with a form string of 0-00 and a fade flag, racing over 10f for the first time after struggling at shorter on Tapeta — this looks a step up in trip with little evidence it will stay, and the redistribution into midfield does it no favours tactically.

runners_data.name: Ibiza Lights
runners_data.note: De Sousa takes the ride for Michael Bell on a 3-year-old who has faded in finishes and shown only one placed effort on good ground in four runs — the hold-up style mapped to midfield adds a positional headache, though the booking of a top-five jockey is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Mist Of Time
runners_data.note: Knight's 3-year-old has a fade flag and a form string of 005-8, but a 22-day turnaround and trainer strike-rate of 1/11 over 14 days shows the yard is in modest nick; the step up from 7-8f to 10f is the key question, and it must prove it truly gets the trip.

runners_data.name: Raise The Stakes
runners_data.note: Redistributed from a hold-up base to the front because no natural front-runner exists — at 8 days' freshness, Fallon aboard, and a second place last time at this trip on good ground, it has form to suggest it can lead and sustain, though its natural style makes the lead role less than certain to be comfortable.

runners_data.name: Shabu Shabu
runners_data.note: Has won over 10f on soft and placed multiple times at this distance, and a 62-day break with a 5lb claiming apprentice (Vigors) is worth monitoring — the form profile on good ground is best of the mid-division group, and it has the experience at the trip to track the pace effectively.

races.paceDynamic: Raise The Stakes is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 1m2f handicap, redistributed to the lead from a hold-up base, meaning the early tempo will be controlled and unhurried rather than genuinely contested. With no natural front-runner to challenge for position, Raise The Stakes is likely to bowl along at a comfortable, sustainable clip on good-to-firm ground, setting a falsely even gallop that compresses the field rather than stringing it out. Zafaan, Ibiza Lights, Sunset In Paris and Rokuni are all genuine hold-up types forced into midfield on the map because there are more closers in this field than the pace shape can accommodate at the rear — in reality, the mid-to-rear division will be crowded, and only the sharpest of them will secure a clean run. A lone, uncontested front-runner on a flat track in good-to-firm conditions with a compressed, hold-up-heavy field behind creates a shape that strongly favours horses who can race prominently just off the pace and sustain their effort — true late closers face a tactical squeeze unless the pace is genuinely honest, which here it may not be.

watchPoints.text: Raise The Stakes (Fallon) — watch whether it actually goes forward from the gates; if it drops in behind, the race loses its only pace-setter and the shape becomes impossible to read.
Zafaan's run-up — 302 days off the track is a serious fitness concern; watch the paddock for signs of race-readiness before treating its good-ground form as reliable.

Crowding risk in the straight — with Rokuni, Sunset In Paris, Zafaan, Ibiza Lights and Hunting Berries all natural hold-up types bunched in the mid-to-rear, there is a real danger of interference or blocked runs on a flat straight track as they all seek gaps simultaneously.

Shabu Shabu's positioning — if Harry Vigors settles it in second or third rather than midfield, its 10f form profile puts it in the best possible place to benefit from a controlled pace set by Raise The Stakes.

Going reassessment — the official going is listed as Good but the going report consistently records Good To Firm across all distances today; horses with firm-ground concerns (Ibiza Lights flagged with headgear 'v') should be monitored for any signs of reluctance or early issues with the faster surface.

runners_data.name: Red Hat Eagle
runners_data.note: A consistent prominent racer who fits this track and trip well; Curtis Wilson-Ruddock (7lb claimer) is worth a small watch, but the horse's seven similar-going runs and strong place record give it legitimate claims from just off the pace, and blinkers suggest it is kept focused.

runners_data.name: Rogue Allegiance
runners_data.note: Harry Davies rides a genuine hold-up type with excellent recent place form over 7f on Good ground — the best recent profile of any closer in the race, 37 days off but no headgear concern, and the Yarmouth straight suits a horse that can finish powerfully.

runners_data.name: Mister Mojito
runners_data.note: Trained by T J Kent with a 66-day break, this horse is a true prominent racer by nature but with five or more pace-seeking types in this field it will be unable to secure its preferred berth, reducing its effectiveness; De Sousa's experience may help it find a workable position but the style fit is compromised.

runners_data.name: Exotic Baby
runners_data.note: George Boughey's 3yo hold-up filly has only one run on similar ground from eight attempts and showed little on that occasion; the step back from 8f to 7f is no obvious boost, and a 16-day turnaround for a horse with limited fast-ground form asks questions.

runners_data.name: Raging Raj
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon partners this 3yo who showed a win and a second over 7-8f on fast ground earlier in the season; form has tailed off but the natural prominent style suits this pace setup and Fallon's tactical awareness could see it organised well early.

runners_data.name: Generous Rascal
runners_data.note: Sean Levey on a 3yo who loves to press from the front; all five recent starts show prominent racing and two placed efforts, though mainly at 6f — the 7f trip on Good to Firm is the slight query, but a 16-day break and an in-form jockey make this one to respect in the pressing group.

runners_data.name: Kimbara
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, Saffie Osborne's mount has a modest but consistent profile over 7-8f on Good ground with four runs this season; Richard Spencer has been striking at 33% over 14 days and Kimbara's ability to lead uncontested is the race's defining tactical fact.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Stevie Donohoe rides a horse that is a natural hold-up type by record — last nine close home — but with the field already packed with rear-of-field horses, this one will be racing in a crowded space for the same late ground; 34 days off and a downward form line (9th last time) make it hard to make a case at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Kimbara is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no direct challenger to her lead, she should bowl along at a fair but manageable tempo over Yarmouth's flat 7f on Good to Firm ground. Red Hat Eagle and Raging Raj will look to press from prominent positions, giving Kimbara some company without likely overwhelming her, while Generous Rascal is another who will try to sit in the first half of the field. The field actually contains more horses that want to race prominently than the pace map can accommodate — Mister Mojito is a natural prominent type who will be shuffled back into a midfield role he does not naturally seek, and Ecclefechan, a true hold-up horse, is similarly displaced, meaning neither can be fully trusted to run their race. The resulting shape — a clear leader, a small cluster of pressers tracking just off her, and limited genuine hold-up cover — strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can control the pace and sustain their effort to the line on a flat, unforgiving track.

watchPoints.text: Kimbara (Saffie Osborne) breaks cleanly — if she goes unchallenged to the front from stall 7, the race shape is set within the first furlong and no other runner can replicate her position.

Mister Mojito (De Sousa) may attempt to push forward from the off despite being mapped to midfield — watch whether he can force his way closer to the pace, as that would alter the dynamics around Red Hat Eagle and Raging Raj.

Rogue Allegiance is the only genuine late closer with current form credentials; if the pace is strong early, Harry Davies will be tracking the rail looking for a gap through the field in the final 2f.
Generous Rascal (Levey) is the most likely horse to sit directly behind Kimbara and apply pressure — if Levey moves him up early to share the front, Kimbara's uncontested lead scenario is undermined.

The Good to Firm official going (confirmed for the 12:30 by the going report) suits the front-running and prominent profiles; any horse with a sole similar-ground run or no wins on fast ground, notably Exotic Baby, faces a genuine surface question.

runners_data.name: Sahana
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly trained by David Simcock who drops back to 6f from 7f-8f assignments; has two placed efforts on good ground including a win at 7f on similar, and 53 days off the track may leave her needing this run to find her sharpest form.

runners_data.name: Cameley Days
runners_data.note: De Sousa takes the ride on this hold-up type who wears a hood and arrives on the back of two wins over 5f on good ground; the step back up to 6f is a query but she has run well at the trip before, and her recent course form is a positive.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: Appleby's filly is in form (two seconds from her last two starts) and quick enough to feature, but her instinct to come from off the pace leaves her squeezed out at the back in a field already stacked with closers — she'll need things to fall perfectly from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: Egotistical
runners_data.note: Varian's three-year-old is the sole confirmed pace-setter and has winning form over this exact course and distance on good ground; the STYLE_FIT tag reflects a positional squeeze in an otherwise hold-up-heavy field, but in practice she faces no real front-running rival here and Jack Mitchell can control proceedings.

runners_data.name: Always Perfect
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity stylistically for Charlie Fellowes, running only her fourth career race; all form is at 6f on good or similar ground, she has been placed twice, and Paddy Bradley (claiming allowance) keeps the weight down, though the absence of a clear running style makes her difficult to place tactically.

runners_data.name: Q T Pie
runners_data.note: NON-RUNNER — no assessment applicable.

races.paceDynamic: Egotistical is the confirmed pace-setter here, the only genuine front-runner in a six-runner field, and with Q T Pie a non-runner the early pace pressure is reduced further, meaning she can stride out from the gates and control this entirely on her own terms at a sustainable clip over Yarmouth's flat six furlongs. Always Perfect is an unknown quantity stylistically but is unlikely to challenge for the lead, while Sahana and Cameley Days are both natural hold-up types who will need Egotistical to either capitulate late or set an honest enough tempo to bring them into it. Fantasy Obsessor is a genuine hold-up operator redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is congested with true closers, meaning she is unlikely to secure any positional advantage over her rivals. This race shape — a lone, uncontested front-runner on good-to-firm ground over a flat track — strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles, with Egotistical able to dictate every yard and control the pace to suit herself.

Sahana and Cameley Days both tracking at the rear — watch whether either jockey opts to improve position earlier than expected, as a change of tactics from either could compromise the other's run and leave both horses in each other's way entering the final two furlongs.

Fantasy Obsessor's draw and early positioning — if she ends up sandwiched between Sahana and Cameley Days with no room to manoeuvre, her genuine finishing speed cannot be deployed, making her position on the track in the first half mile critical.

Always Perfect's starting position and early movement — her style is listed as unknown, and if Bradley opts to track Egotistical prominently rather than drop away, she becomes a more significant factor in Scenario A than her current assessment suggests.

runners_data.name: Sir Rodneyredblood
runners_data.note: Returns after a 59-day absence for a yard that has sent out 0/4 runners in the past fortnight, and though it has placed at this level on standard ground, it has struggled on going as quick as Good — a natural hold-up horse that will want to come late, but 0W0P on comparable going and a long layoff make this a risky proposition.

runners_data.name: Valadero
runners_data.note: 165 days off the track is a significant fitness concern, and Brian Toomey's 0/2 recent record compounds that worry; a hold-up horse that has raced consistently at 7f-8f, stepping back to 6f on Good ground is an unknown, and though it has placed on similar going, the extended absence and step in trip reduction make it hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Bear Steps
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Jack Jones, whose yard is in decent form (2/10 in past 14 days), and Cieren Fallon is a significant jockey booking — the horse is a natural hold-up type whose history shows limited form on Good ground (1/5 runs), and stepping back from 7f to 6f is a question, but Fallon's tactical intelligence could see it manufactured into a prominent position in this leaderless field.

runners_data.name: Shining Guest
runners_data.note: All three career runs have come on Good ground so there is genuine going familiarity, and Silvestre De Sousa is the standout jockey booking in this race by some margin — a 3-year-old for George Margarson who has been 0/7 in the past fortnight, the form of 67-6 is modest, but De Sousa's ability to read a muddled pace scenario and deliver a horse at the right moment makes this runner particularly interesting in a falsely-run sprint.

runners_data.name: Wondrous
runners_data.note: Carries a notable "fades in finish" tag which is a serious concern in what is almost certain to be a sprint-finish scenario — Michael Bell's yard has a broad recent record and the 29-day break is fine, but finishing 9th, 12th, 7th and 10th in recent starts on Good ground paints a consistent picture of a horse that simply cannot sustain its effort when the race truly ignites, making this the most vulnerable runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: This is an unusual 6f sprint at Yarmouth in which every single runner carries a hold-up profile — there is no confirmed front-runner in the field, meaning the early gallop is entirely uncertain and likely to be pedestrian until horses are forced wide or into unfamiliar territory. With all six runners naturally wanting to settle and come from off the pace, the race will almost certainly drift into a muddled, slowly-run affair before igniting in the final two furlongs, producing a sprint finish with little tactical shape to speak of. Bear Steps, Valadero, Coolagh Magic and Sir Rodneyredblood have all been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply more hold-up types than the race geometry can accommodate at the rear — in practice, whoever breaks sharpest will be pressed into a lead or prominent position they do not naturally seek. The tactical verdict is clear: with no genuine pace-setter, this race shape favours whichever runner can produce the sharpest late acceleration in a compressed, sprint-finish scenario — but given everyone wants that role, the horse with the best recent form, the shrewdest jockey, and the ability to handle a falsely-run 6f will be best placed; Silvestre De Sousa on Shining Guest and Cieren Fallon on Bear Steps are the riders most likely to manufacture position from the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Shining Guest (De Sousa) to be positioned just off the non-existent pace — in a field of hold-up types with no front-runner, De Sousa will know to manufacture track position early and could be in the ideal slot approaching the final furlong.

Bear Steps ridden by Fallon could be nudged into an unplanned lead given the absence of any natural front-runner — if Fallon takes that option deliberately, it becomes a very different proposition and one to track closely from the gate.

Wondrous carries a "fades in finish" flag and this race is almost certain to end in a sprint — back it to capitulate in the closing stages and potentially cause interference as it weakens through the field in the final 100 yards.

Valadero's 165-day absence means its fitness is unverified; a stale hold-up horse that cannot travel into the race at Yarmouth's tight six-furlong test could be a non-factor throughout, but watch it in the paddock for signs of well-being before dismissing.

With all six runners carrying hold-up profiles, monitor the early stalls break closely — the horse that is fastest away could find itself in front before its rider intends, and that accidental leader will shape the entire race if it can dictate even a modest tempo.
